questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

It has becoming clear (1)/ that attempts to impress the (2)/ people have failed. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Correct option:**1)** Since the latter part of the sentence conveys that the attempts have already failed, the error is in the first part of the sentence** (has becoming).** The correct form of the verb **‘become’** should be **‘has become’.**

Thus the correct sentence is:

*It **has become **clear that attempts to impress the people have failed.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

A raise is important (1)/ since one had to beat (2)/ rising prices. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Correct option: **2)**The error lies in the **second part **of the sentence. The usage of** ‘had’** is incorrect as the sentence is in the **present tense**. The correct word to be used is **‘has’**.

Therefore, the correct sentence is:

*A raise is important since one** has **to beat rising prices.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

We are committed in providing (1)/ you a safe and (2)/ comfortable travel experience. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution: Here the correct answer is **1.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** __ • The fault is in** part 1 **of the sentence due to the presence of preposition **‘in’**. • The verb committed takes the preposition** ‘to’** with it. • For Example - Jana won an academic award after **committing herself to** her studies. • Thus, the correct answer is **Option 1.** Hence, the correct sentence is: *We are **committed to** providing you a safe and comfortable travel experience.* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **Hinglish__** • Preposition 'in' की उपस्थिति के कारण वाक्य के भाग 1 में दोष है। • Verb 'committed' के साथ preposition 'to' का उपयोग होता है। • उदाहरण के लिए - Jana won an academic award after **committing herself to** her studies. • अत: सही उत्तर **विकल्प 1** है। अत: सही वाक्य है: We are **committed to **providing you a safe and comfortable travel experience. 52:Tc1e, The correct answer is **2**.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Most of us have a (1)/ desire to create wealth in the (2)/ shortest period in time. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Correct option: 3) The flaw is in the third part of the sentence. The fault is due to the presence of** preposition ‘in’**. It is always a** ‘period of time’.**

Hence, the correct sentence is:

*Most of us have a desire to create wealth in the shortest period **of** time.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Intrigued by this (1)/ problem, I began search (2)/ for a solution. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **2**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Using **'searching'** in the place of **'search'** to make the sentence correct.
 
• **'Began' **is the 2nd form of the verb **'Begin'**, we know that after the verb 'began' needs the objective case of **'noun or pronoun'**. 
 
• **'Searching'** is the **gerund form** of the verb **'Search'** and we know that gerund can act as a noun. So it is the most suitable here.
 
• Hence, **option 2 **is the most appropriate answer here.**
 

The correct sentence is:* Intrigued by this problem, I began **searching** for a solution. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A gerund** is the **'–ing'** form of a verb that functions the same as a noun.

 
 
• **For ****example**, 'Running is fun.' *(In this sentence, **'running'** is the ****gerund**. It acts just like a noun)*

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **4**.

__
 
• The sentence is grammatically and contextually correct.
 
• Hence, there is** no error **in the sentence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• In first part of the sentence "is" is used correctly. Here "is" comes for something. In this structure "there' is used as an introductory there, so first part of the sentence is correct.
 
• In second part of the sentence the "in the store for" is also correct because it gives the contextual meaning of the sentence and here preposition 'for' is also correct.
 
• In third part of sentence only one word i.e. "everyone", itself correct to the contextual sense of the sentence.

questions.question:
**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Travel blogging is hardly work (1)/ and will earn you nothing (2)/ in the first few years. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Correct option**: 1)‘Hardly’ **is incorrectly used in first part of the sentence as it is used to qualify a statement by saying that it is true to an insignificant degree. The correct form to be used is **‘hard’** as it means requiring a great deal of endurance or effort.

The correct sentence is:

*Travel blogging is** hard** work and will earn you nothing in the first few years.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Since 1975, there (was) no volcanic eruptions.
questions.solution:
Correct option: **3)**The phrase in bracketed part must be replaced with **‘have been’** because we use the** present perfect continuous** to talk about repeated activities which started at a particular time in the past and are still continuing till now.

Therefore, the correct sentence is:

*Since 1975, there **have been** no volcanic eruptions.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Joyce could not help (crying).
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **No improvement.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**:-

__
 
• In the above given sentence, **'crying'** will be used.
 
• We either use **'could not help but + infinitive (V1 = base form of the verb)' **or** (could not help + gerund 'V1 + ing').**
 
• **For Example:- **
 
 
• Mayank could not help but study.
 
• Mayank could not help studying.
 
 
 
• So it can either be:-
 
 
• **'Joyce could not help crying.'** or** 'Joyce could not help but cry.'**
 
 
 
• **'But crying'** is wrong here.
 
• **'Could not help' **is followed by a **gerund(V₊ᵢₙg).**

**Hence, the correct sentence is ***Joyce could not help **crying.***

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__** 

*If we use the conjunction 'but' after the verb phrase 'could not help', **the verb which would follow would take the base(V1) form. ***

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

I met a gentleman, (who I believe to be a) actor.

options.text: who, to my belief, must be an

questions.solution:
Correct option: **3)**The phrase in the bracket must be replaced with **‘who'**, to my belief, must be **'an’** to make the sentence grammatically correct.

In option 1** 'who **believe, is an' is **wrong** as it suggests that the gentleman believes and not the speaker.

In option 2 'whom I believe, is **a**' is **wrong **because an is the wrong article to be used here. The word actor starts with a vowel sound and needs the article '**an**' before it. 

Therefore, the correct sentence would be:

*I met a gentleman, **who**, **to my belief, must be an** actor*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Long after (you have done talking), maintain good eye contact.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is:** ****You are done talking**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The use of the verb 'maintain' is in the **present indefinite **tense.
 
• As the latter part of the sentence is in the **present indefinite tense**, the part of the sentence that needs improvement must also be in the **present indefinite tense**.
 
• This grammatical innuendo is used to draw **parallelism** between the two tense structures of the sentence.
 
• Only option (2) is in the present indefinite form.
 
• Option (3) is also in the present indefinite form, but the use of the be verb 'am' after 'you' is grammatically incorrect.

Therefore, the corrected form of the sentence is:* Long after **you are done talking**, maintain good eye contact.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

The foreign minister said that maintaining cordial relations with our neighbour (becomes the key).
questions.solution:
Correct option: **3)**The phrase in the bracket must be replaced with **‘is the key**’ to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Here in this sentence maintaining cordial relation is of the utmost importance, **brings the key** and **hold the key** doesn't make any sense, only **is the** **key **here signifies that it is the essential thing which is required

Therefore, the correct sentence would be:

*The foreign minister said that maintaining cordial relations with our neighbour **is the key.***

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

(Those) Diwali celebration was wonderful.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"That"**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence, "Those" is incorrect instead of this we need to use "that".
 
• "Those" is a plural form of "this" hence, it is incorrect to use it because "Celebration" is singular.
 
• Also, we can't use "these" as it is a plural form too.
 
• "Thing" is a noun that is not suitable as it is out of context hence, the correct pronoun is "that".
 
• "That" is used to refer to a person or thing, especially when he/she/it is not near the person speaking.

**So the correct sentence is-** *That Diwali Celebration was wonderful.*

questions.question:
**In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the bracketed part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select "no improvement".**

Raman as well as Amar (are) coming.
questions.solution:
‘Are’ must be replaced by ‘is’ because when ‘as well as’ is used to combine two subjects, **the verb agrees with the subject mentioned first.**

Therefore, the correct sentence is:

Ram as well as Amar is coming.

questions.question:
**In the following question, the sentence is given with blank to be filled in with an appropriate word. Select the correct alternative out of the four and indicate it by selecting the appropriate option.**

_______ was well arranged.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** "Everything".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the given sentence everything is used for 'things' that have been arranged properly. It gives the contextual meaning of the sentence.
 
• 'Anything' will not be used as 'Anything was well arranged' does not gives the sense of the sentence.
 
• Everyone is used only for people, never animals or objects. So in the given sentence everyone will not be used, as the given sentence talks about 'things' that was well arranged.
 
• The pronoun "none" means not one, not any, or no persons or things. None could be used but the sentence will give the negative sense.
 
• The correct sentence is **"Everything was well arranged."**

Hence, from the above statement it is clear that the correct answer is** "Option 1".**

options.text: Author never has and never will give on itinerary in his/her blog.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the passage, the author has stated clearly that they "never have and never will give you a three-day itinerary to 'do' a destination."
 
• The author feels that their job as a travel blogger is to inspire readers to think of travel differently, to make their own journey rather than follow a set itinerary.

Therefore, the correct answer is '**Option 1**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Though the author talks about walking on cobblestoned streets in Istria, it is not explicitly mentioned that Istria is full of such streets. Hence, option 2 is not correct.
 
• The author does express their concerns about day-trippers intruding into the life of the locals. However, the passage doesn't explicitly generalize that day-trippers are always intruding. So, option 3 is not fully correct.
 
• While the author discusses the impact of travel blogging on offbeat places, they don't assert that travel blogging always ruins such places. In fact, the author argues they could inspire people to travel differently. Hence, option 4 is not correct.

__
 
• Context of the Passage: The passage focuses on the author’s reflection about the impact of revealing offbeat travel destinations to a wide audience.
 
• Conflict Description: The author mentions their dilemma explicitly, discussing the pros and cons of sharing these hidden gems.
 
• Role of a Travel Blogger: The author deliberates on whether a travel blogger's responsibility includes disclosing exact locations.
 
• Outcome: The realization that sharing exact locations may not always be beneficial forms the crux of the author's long-held dilemma.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option **1.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
